sections.title: The Founder Emperor's Tomb
sections.body: Gia Long was the first emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty, which ruled from Hue after the city became Vietnam's imperial capital in 1802. His tomb sits far from the center, where hills, water, courtyards, and stone guardians make the visit read more like a landscape than a single building.

sections.title: Why The Distance Matters
sections.body: This is one of Hue's more remote royal tombs, so the ride is part of the decision. Choose it when the day can handle the trip out and back.

sections.title: Water, Hills, Stone Guardians
sections.body: Expect a spread-out tomb landscape: paths, courtyards, lakes or ponds, low hills, and guardian figures. The setting carries as much meaning as the structures.

sections.title: Quieter Than The Famous Tombs
sections.body: Compared with Minh Mang or Tu Duc, Gia Long is quieter and more open. It is a good choice when the appeal is space, history, and fewer people around you.

sections.title: Transport Comes First
